governing_rule: No decorative statistics. Every number, chart, table, or map must answer a question the reader is likely to have at that point in the text.

skip.GOOGLE_CIVIC: PARTIAL — IP-restricted on agent runtime; do not publish empty contest counts as evidence.
skip.OPENFEC_API_CAPPED_SERIES: API sample capped at ~200 candidates/cycle; do not substitute for CC-IND-D04 weball baseline (73%).

panels.title: Political money and legislative observability
panels.reader_question: How concentrated is congressional campaign funding, and what legislative structure is actually observable?
panels.strength_note: Strong for disclosure/observability of candidate-receipt concentration (CC-IND-D04). Partial/not enough evidence for causal capture (CC-CLAIM-003).

what_the_data_show.key_finding: In the 2023–2024 FEC weball universe, the top tenth of House and Senate candidates with receipts held about 73% of those candidates’ aggregate receipts.

critical_numbers.label: Top-decile share of HS candidate receipts
Candidates with receipts > 0 in weball file
Arkansas officeholders returned by Open States
critical_numbers.note: Roster aggregate (99 lower / 35 upper / 8 executive in retrieved roles) — not a performance or capture score.

critical_numbers.label: Recent Arkansas bill sample (Open States)
critical_numbers.note: Targeted sample, not a full session warehouse.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Federal disclosure makes candidate-receipt concentration measurable. That observability supports honesty about political money; it does not by itself prove that economic concentration weakens democratic accountability.

what_supports_this: FEC weball bulk file computation for CC-IND-D04 (CC-SRC-257).
RedDirt credential-free legislative/civic export exp_legciv_9ab7ba9f3266 (Open States AR roster/bills; Congress.gov samples).
CC-CLAIM-134: disclosure systems make large political-money flows publicly observable.
what_challenges_it: Disclosure is not capture (CC-CLAIM-003 opposing evidence; CC-CLAIM-134).
Candidate-receipt concentration is not donor-level concentration and excludes presidential and IE-only committees.
Open States bill volume ≠ legislative scrutiny; roster ≠ influence.
Branham/Soroka/Wlezien and related literatures contest strong oligarchy readings when preferences diverge.
what_we_dont_know: Causal identification from concentration → weakened accountability remains open (CC-CLAIM-003).
Google Civic contest/election structure for controlled AR places is not yet publishable from this runtime (IP restriction).
Multi-cycle weball series beyond the 2023–2024 baseline slot is not yet bound on this panel.

panels.title: Arkansas demographic context for community laboratories
panels.reader_question: What statewide demographic backdrop surrounds Arkansas Living Community Laboratory cases?
panels.strength_note: ACS state aggregates are context only — not community baselines and not causal proof of local outcomes.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Arkansas ACS 2023 5-year estimates place state population near 3.03 million and median household income near $58,773 — useful statewide context, not a Rose Bud or Lewisville community baseline.

critical_numbers.label: Open States AR legislator roster count

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Statewide ACS numbers answer ‘what kind of state context are these cases inside?’ They do not answer whether a local school, farm, or resource project will succeed.

what_supports_this: Census ACS 5-year via RedDirt targeted ingest (exp_legciv_9ab7ba9f3266).
Open States Arkansas people endpoint roster aggregate.
what_challenges_it: State aggregates hide rural/urban and county differences.
Socioeconomic context ≠ political causation.
LEARNS / local funding questions remain open and must not be filled with statewide averages.
what_we_dont_know: Community-specific baselines for Rose Bud and Lewisville Parts I–VI are not started.
Place-level contest/election administration structure awaits Google Civic re-run from an IP-allowed machine.

panels.title: Observable political-money concentration (comparison pages)
panels.reader_question: When a comparison dossier talks about money translating into political control, what concentration figure is actually measured today?
panels.strength_note: Strong for measurable candidate-receipt concentration; does not prove plutocracy or capture as a regime type.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Candidate-receipt concentration is measurable: top-decile House/Senate candidates held about 73% of aggregate receipts among candidates with receipts > 0 in the 2023–2024 FEC weball file.

critical_numbers.label: Top-decile share of HS candidate receipts

what_the_data_show.plain_english: This answers a measurement question on political-money concentration among congressional candidates. It does not license labeling the United States a plutocracy or proving national capture.

what_challenges_it: Receipt concentration ≠ donor oligarchy and ≠ policy capture.
Comparative dossiers remain analytical tools, not settled regime classifications.
what_we_dont_know: Cross-national comparable series and donor-level concentration are not bound here.

panels.title: Outlet presence vs institutional scrutiny (Arkansas 90-day sample)
panels.reader_question: Does having a local newspaper mean public institutions are being watched?
panels.strength_note: Strong for the negative finding that outlet presence ≠ sustained institutional scrutiny in this window. Not a journalism quality score.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Across six Arkansas pilot geographies in a 90-day digital window (2026-05-12→2026-08-10), nominal outlet presence did not predict sustained independent original scrutiny of public institutions. Searcy shows an institutional-coverage desert despite a paper.

critical_numbers.label: Composite journalism score
critical_numbers.note: Project forbids collapsing coverage into a single score.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: A newspaper can exist and still publish almost no original scrutiny of Quorum Court, city council, or school-board decisions. Outlet presence answers a distribution question; institutional coverage answers a democracy question.

what_challenges_it: Window is 90 days and digital-sample limited
Paywalled/archive gaps inflate UNKNOWN cells
Lafayette site 503 / insufficient archive
what_we_dont_know: Statewide Arkansas journalism map beyond six geos
Whether financing reforms raise institutional coverage

panels.title: Arkansas livestock processing: capacity somewhere ≠ usable access
panels.reader_question: Is Clinton a USDA livestock processing hub, and do family farmers have practical inspected pathways?
panels.strength_note: Strong for falsifying the Clinton USDA-livestock-hub claim and for the access≠capacity posture. Booking/usable economics remain unverified (0/0).

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Clinton is not a proven regional USDA-inspected livestock processing hub. FSIS extract shows no Meat Slaughter establishment in Van Buren County; Cypress Valley is custom-exempt. Arkansas has inspected plants — that is not the same as practical family-farm access.

critical_numbers.label: Desk-accessible inspected cattle pathways
critical_numbers.note: Booking confirmation 0; economically usable confirmation 0 — zeros mean not yet verified.

critical_numbers.label: CC-CLAIM-138 posture
critical_numbers.note: Processing-bottleneck clause strengthened; monopsony magnitudes still unmeasured.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Arkansas often has physical capacity somewhere in the system, but independent producers may lack practical access on usable terms. Do not invent booking times or build new plants from desk inference alone.

what_challenges_it: Custom-exempt pathways exist but are not retail USDA pathways
Poultry MPI/commercial conflicts remain NEE
National packer concentration literature is separate from AR access maps

last_updated.dataset_or_release: AR ag posture lock + Clinton hub FSIS test

panels.title: Sectoral influence ladder (not a capture shortcut)
panels.reader_question: When sector dossiers talk about political money and regulation, what level of claim is actually earned?
panels.strength_note: Partial/associational at sector level. Capture bar not met for a national canonical capture claim.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Preserve the ladder: Activity → Access → Association → Influence → Capture. Telecom shows associational contribution–outcome patterns; electric utilities have a provisional quasi-experimental working-paper candidate; none currently clears a CC capture bar. National candidate-receipt concentration (73%) is observability, not sector capture.

critical_numbers.label: Electric utilities capture bar
critical_numbers.note: Working-paper DiD — do not promote capture from WP alone.

critical_numbers.label: Agriculture sectoral capture bar
critical_numbers.note: AR access research ≠ national capture proof.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Sector evidence can document political activity and associations without proving that an industry owns its regulators. Keep verbs honest.

what_challenges_it: Working papers are not peer-settled facts
Arkansas-specific regulator modules mostly future work
Branham et al. contest strong oligarchy readings

panels.title: Household wealth concentration (baseline)
panels.reader_question: How concentrated is U.S. household wealth on official Fed products?
panels.strength_note: Strong for measured concentration levels/shares. Does not prove oligarchy as regime type or that CC redesign would shift ownership.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Official Fed products show high household wealth concentration with important product caveats: 2022 SCF median net worth about $192,900; 2026-Q1 DFA shares place the bottom 50% near 5.3% and the top 1% near 28.8%.
what_the_data_show.plain_english: Wealth is highly concentrated on official series. SCF levels and DFA shares are not interchangeable. Concentration is a factual predicate for later accountability questions — not proof of oligarchy or of a finished CC remedy.

what_challenges_it: 2019–2022 SCF narrowing episode
Middle 40% still ~31% share
Method differences change extremes

panels.title: Public trust and baseline readiness dial
panels.reader_question: How thin is measured public trust, and how complete is the national baseline?
panels.strength_note: Strong for the trust series reading and baseline completeness dial. Trust ≠ capture; baseline completeness ≠ theory completion.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: About 15.4% say they trust the government in Washington always/most of the time (2024). National baseline slots are 42/64 sourced — enough for data-dense publication in many domains, not enough to declare diagnosis finished.
what_the_data_show.plain_english: Low trust and incomplete baselines are reasons for humility: publish the strongest available numbers beside theory, and keep unknowns visible.

what_challenges_it: Survey trust items are not institutional performance scores
42/64 leaves major democracy/justice slots thin

panels.title: Public finance of local news — dollars ≠ scrutiny
panels.reader_question: If public money can fund journalism projects, does that prove institutional coverage or durable independence?
panels.strength_note: Strong for appropriation volatility and the chain-of-inference ban; Partial/NEE for durable capacity and civic outcomes. Citizen-directed Civic Information Credits remain Not Enough Evidence.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: NJ Civic Information Consortium shows a real public-finance pathway with claimed statutory editorial firewalls — and appropriation volatility that can go to zero (FY2027 $0 in the budget-aggregator series). Money appropriated ≠ journalism produced ≠ institutions covered ≠ civic outcomes.

critical_numbers.label: NJ CIC FY2027 appropriated (aggregator series)
critical_numbers.note: Conflict with program case-study narrative retained; neither preferred without primary PDF reconciliation.

critical_numbers.label: NJ CIC grants claimed (self-report)
critical_numbers.note: Self-report — not an independent institutional-coverage audit.

critical_numbers.label: Citizen-directed Civic Information Credits
critical_numbers.note: No US news-voucher pilot; Seattle Democracy Vouchers are campaign-finance analogy only.

critical_numbers.label: Arkansas institutional-coverage composite score
critical_numbers.note: Financing dossiers must not invent a journalism quality score.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Public finance can move dollars through a nonprofit intermediary. That does not prove beat continuity, institutional scrutiny, or survival under hostile appropriators. Do not prescribe financing where Arkansas-style institutional coverage remains unknown.

what_challenges_it: Two conflicting NJ funding series (aggregator vs case study)
Statutory firewall ≠ purse immunity
Self-reported stories/jobs ≠ institutions covered
what_we_dont_know: Independent longitudinal employment/beat continuity under CIC
Hostile-government survival for every public-money path
Whether any financing model raises Arkansas institutional coverage

panels.title: Recent wage growth and productivity (baseline dials)
panels.reader_question: Have wages and productivity moved together recently, and what do the official dials actually measure?
panels.strength_note: Strong for recent official dials (L01/L02). Historical productivity–compensation gap remains a separate BLS/EPI evidence track; EPI secondary must not stand alone. Not a causal capture finding.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: A small labor dial system — not a single headline — shows real AHE +1.1% (to Dec 2025), productivity +2.3% (2024), and voluntary quits 2.1% (2024), beside a longer BLS-documented productivity–compensation gap whose magnitude remains contested.

critical_numbers.label: Real AHE over-the-year change (CES)
critical_numbers.note: Mean AHE of private nonfarm jobs, CPI-U deflated.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Readers should see definition, comparison, and series status — not treat 1.1% as the whole labor story.

what_challenges_it: L01 is mean AHE of jobs, not median/typical-worker pay
EPI gap magnitudes are secondary and methodology-sensitive
Causal attribution remains debated
what_we_dont_know: Official post-2015 industry gap update tables not attached

evidence_system.definition: L01 = 12-month % change in real average hourly earnings (CES, CPI-U). L02 = annual % change in nonfarm-business labor productivity (BLS). L04 = JOLTS annual-average voluntary quits rate.

comparison.label: Recent wage dial vs productivity dial
comparison.note: Different concepts/years — not a causal gap estimate.

comparison.label: Voluntary quits rate (mobility proxy)
comparison.note: Quits ≠ job-to-job flows; not Census J2J.

comparison.label: Long-run productivity–compensation gap
comparison.note: EPI secondary series must stay labeled secondary.

evidence_system.series_note: Official historical series exist at BLS for AHE, productivity, and JOLTS. Multi-year point arrays are not yet attached in-repo; Pass 4 publishes the dial system + series status, not a chart warehouse.
evidence_system.qualification: L01 is mean AHE of jobs, not median/typical-worker pay. One-year dials do not close the post-1970s shared-gains debate.

panels.title: Antitrust enforcement activity (criminal cases filed)
panels.reader_question: How much criminal antitrust enforcement is actually filed, and what does that count not prove?
panels.strength_note: Strong for the administrative count. Not a concentration index, not consumer-harm proof, and not political capture.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: DOJ Antitrust Division filed 20 criminal antitrust cases in FY2024. That answers an enforcement-activity question. It does not measure economy-wide concentration, FTC activity, civil merger outcomes, or capture of competition policy.

critical_numbers.label: DOJ ATR criminal cases filed
critical_numbers.note: Criminal cases only — excludes FTC and DOJ civil/non-criminal merger actions.

critical_numbers.label: Census concentration products
critical_numbers.note: Keep industry CR cells; do not invent a fake national concentration percent.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Enforcement counts and industry concentration ratios are measurement outputs. Neither alone proves monopoly, consumer harm, or that laissez-faire (or any rival system) is vindicated or refuted.

what_challenges_it: Case counts are not rates per firm or per merger
Product-market definition changes apparent concentration
No automatic finding of harm or capture
what_we_dont_know: Fixed-NAICS multi-year CR comparison table not yet in-repo
Labor-market concentration datasets not bound here

panels.title: Federal fiscal dials (revenue, spending, debt)
panels.reader_question: What federal revenue, spending, and debt dials exist today — and what do they not prove about a no-personal-income-tax / no-property-tax redesign?
panels.strength_note: Strong for federal CBO budget identities. Does not validate or falsify a state/local no-PIT/no-property-tax prosperity model; those modules remain open.

evidence_system.definition: G01 = federal receipts % GDP (FY). G02 = federal outlays % GDP (FY). G03 = federal debt held by the public % GDP. All federal — not state/local tax capacity.

comparison.label: Receipts vs outlays (FY2024)
comparison.note: Gap is a fiscal identity, not a tax-incidence model.

comparison.label: Debt held by the public
comparison.note: Outlook vintages revise; later vintages may show ~100% for 2025.

comparison.label: CBO household distribution (2021)
comparison.note: Distributional fact for 2021; pandemic-year effects matter. Not a property-tax module.

evidence_system.series_note: CBO historical budget identities are official series. Multi-year point arrays not yet attached in-repo.
evidence_system.qualification: These dials do not prove a no-personal-income-tax / no-property-tax redesign is feasible. Destination-based tax and property-tax modules remain research-open. Do not invent state revenue replacement paths.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Federal fiscal dials show receipts about 17.1% of GDP, outlays 23.4%, and debt held by the public near 99% of GDP (FY2024/2024). Separately, CBO’s 2021 household distribution shows large pre-tax gaps compressed by transfers and federal taxes without elimination.

critical_numbers.label: Debt held by the public % GDP
CBO Q5/Q1 income ratio after transfers/taxes
critical_numbers.note: Household distribution snapshot — not a tax redesign scorecard.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Publish the federal fiscal system beside any prosperity-tax claim. Compression of inequality by today’s federal taxes/transfers is real; that is not proof that removing personal income or property taxes would preserve public capacity.

what_challenges_it: Federal-only identities miss state/local and property-tax structure
2021 distribution includes pandemic credits and elevated capital gains
No completed revenue-replacement model for no-PIT/no-property-tax

panels.title: Ownership and retirement participation system
panels.reader_question: Who owns assets and retirement accounts today — and what does that imply for capital-participation designs?
panels.strength_note: Strong for ownership/participation snapshots. Ownership ≠ adequacy; employee-ownership baseline (L03) still pending.

evidence_system.definition: W01 SCF median net worth; W02 DFA wealth shares; W04 homeownership rate; W05 share of families with retirement accounts (SCF).
evidence_system.series_note: SCF triennial and DFA quarterly products exist officially. In-repo attachment is snapshot composition + participation rates, not a multi-decade chart pack yet.
evidence_system.qualification: Do not treat retirement-account ownership as proof of secure aging, or wealth concentration as proof of oligarchy. Employee/local ownership magnitudes remain thin (L03 pending).

what_the_data_show.key_finding: A small ownership system shows high wealth concentration, majority but incomplete homeownership, and only about 54.3% of families holding retirement accounts — the empirical backdrop for civic-wealth and prosperous-aging designs.
what_the_data_show.plain_english: Capital-participation claims should sit on this system. Participation gaps are real; redesign benefits are not measured here.

what_challenges_it: SCF levels ≠ DFA shares
Retirement ownership ≠ adequacy
2019–2022 SCF narrowing episode

panels.title: Rural structure and local capital-access system
panels.reader_question: What measurable rural and local-capital structure surrounds community-prosperity claims?
panels.strength_note: Strong for structural dials. Statewide/national ≠ local community baselines. SBCS is applicant approval among employer firms, not a population access rate.

evidence_system.definition: CM02 = Census rural population share. CM04 = FDIC community-bank deposit share. E01 = community-bank + credit-union loan share. E02 = SBCS full-approval rate + USDA FSA farm-loan obligations.

comparison.label: SBCS full approval / FSA farm-loan obligations
comparison.note: Two different instruments — do not collapse into one score.

evidence_system.series_note: FDIC QBP and Census urban/rural products are official. In-repo points are single-period snapshots; label statewide ≠ local.
evidence_system.qualification: These are national structural dials for rural/local capital context. They do not measure a specific Arkansas town’s prosperity account, hospital access (CM03 deferred), or leakage.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: About one-fifth of the U.S. population is Census-rural; community banks hold about 13.1% of domestic deposits; community banks plus credit unions hold about 24.9% of depository loans; SBCS full approval was 52% among employer-firm applicants while FSA farm-loan obligations were about $5.39B in FY2024.
what_the_data_show.plain_english: Local-ownership and community-prosperity pages need this structural system beside design claims — labeled as national context, not town outcomes.

what_challenges_it: Census rural ≠ OMB nonmetro
SBCS applicant universe ≠ all firms
FSA is farm credit, not general rural SMB credit
what_we_dont_know: SBA 7(a)/504 dollar series still pending primary retrieval

panels.title: Market dynamics: entry and enforcement (not a competitiveness score)
panels.reader_question: Beyond 20 criminal antitrust cases, what else is measurable about market dynamics — and what still is not?
panels.strength_note: Strong for entry count + criminal enforcement count. Weak/Partial as a competitiveness measure — industry CR sample cells and multi-year CR tables are not yet bound.

evidence_system.definition: C02 = Census BDS establishments born in the last 12 months. C03 = DOJ ATR criminal antitrust cases filed (FY). Census concentration products report industry CR shares — not a national concentration percent.

comparison.label: New establishment entrants (BDS)
comparison.note: Dynamics count — not survival or markups.

comparison.label: Industry concentration (Economic Census)
comparison.note: C01 object exists; sample CR table not attached.

evidence_system.series_note: BDS and DOJ ATR tables are official series. Fixed-NAICS multi-year CR comparison table is still missing in-repo.
evidence_system.qualification: Do not treat 20 criminal cases as a competitiveness score. Do not invent a national CR4. Entry counts and enforcement counts answer different reader questions.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Market-dynamics evidence currently supports an entry dial (≈790k new establishments in 2023) and an enforcement dial (20 DOJ ATR criminal cases in FY2024). Neither is a concentration index; industry CR products remain cell-based.

critical_numbers.label: National concentration percent
critical_numbers.note: Keep industry CR cells; do not invent a fake national %.

what_the_data_show.plain_english: Pass 4 upgrades competition surfaces from a single enforcement headline into a two-dial system with an explicit CR gap.

what_challenges_it: Entrants ≠ competitive intensity
Criminal cases exclude FTC and civil merger actions
Product-market definition changes CR readings
what_we_dont_know: In-repo sample CR4 table for fixed NAICS

panels.title: Primary-care access shortage (HPSA)
panels.reader_question: Where healthcare prose talks about access, what shortage dial is actually measured?
panels.strength_note: Strong for the HPSA population-share proxy; Partial because designation ≠ utilization, and mental-health HPSAs are separate.

evidence_system.definition: E05 ≈ share of U.S. population residing in designated primary-care Health Professional Shortage Areas (HRSA).

comparison.label: Hospital-access baseline (CM03)
comparison.note: Do not substitute HPSA for hospital access.

evidence_system.series_note: HRSA designations update ongoing; multi-year share array not attached in-repo.
evidence_system.qualification: Do not let health-system design prose outrun this thin but honest dial. Insurance concentration and drug-pricing slots remain unsourced.

what_the_data_show.key_finding: About 22% of the U.S. population lives in designated primary-care HPSAs (2024-06-30 HRSA reading). That is an access-shortage proxy — not a completed healthcare diagnosis.
what_the_data_show.plain_english: Put the shortage dial beside rural-health and community-care claims; keep unknowns about insurance, prevention investment, and hospital access visible.

what_challenges_it: Designation ≠ care received
Mental-health HPSAs separate
Rural hospital measures deferred

panels.title: Apprenticeship and early-adult pathway dials
panels.reader_question: What measurable apprenticeship and early-adult ownership/civic dials sit beside academy and CTE design claims?
panels.strength_note: Strong for administrative/survey dials. Not Arkansas CTE outcomes and not academy pilot results.

evidence_system.definition: L05 = active registered apprentices (all ages). HC02 = RAPIDS youth (16–24) total served. HC06 = homeownership among householders under 35. HC07 = CPS voting rate ages 18–24.
evidence_system.series_note: DOL RAPIDS and ACS/CPS products are official. Arkansas CTE matrices exist in research/ but are not substituted here as national academy outcomes.
evidence_system.qualification: Pathway dials ≠ regional academy success. Do not invent graduate retention or early-career earnings by pathway (HC04/HC05 pending).

what_the_data_show.key_finding: Registered apprenticeship is large in absolute terms (~680k active; ~353k youth served), while young-adult homeownership is about 36.1% and 18–24 citizen voting about 47.7% — empirical dials for human-capital pages that currently lean design-heavy.
what_the_data_show.plain_english: Academy and CTE design should sit beside pathway dials and keep Arkansas-specific outcome claims separately labeled until attached.

what_challenges_it: Registered only — not all WBL
Youth total served ≠ active stock
Householder-based ownership measure
what_we_dont_know: AR CTE → wage alignment series not bound here

pass_summary.note: Evidence-desert hunt; small evidence systems preferred; energy deferred (no sourced baseline metrics).

pass_4_rule: Prefer a small evidence system over isolated headline numbers whenever the data permit it (definition + comparison + series status + qualification + source).
